name: Elizabeth Philp
residence: Hidden Valley, between Riverton and Shoshoni, Fremont County (moved there in 1994 from Lysite; 2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
occupation: Rancher; she wrote that she and her husband own a small farm and raise cattle in Hidden Valley (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
education: Shoshoni High School; Casper College; B.S. in agricultural business, University of Wyoming, 1981; Wyoming LEAD Program (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
background: In her 2024 WyoFile questionnaire, Elizabeth Philp wrote that she lived on Hidden Valley Road between Riverton and Shoshoni, having moved there in 1994 from Lysite; that she had lived in Wyoming 65 years and was born in Riverton; and that she would be 66 on Election Day 2024.

She wrote that she was raised by her parents, John and Ann Philp, on the family ranch at Lysite, worked on the ranch growing up, graduated from Shoshoni, Casper College, and the University of Wyoming (B.S. in agricultural business, 1981), and returned to ranch work after college. She said she participated in the Wyoming LEAD Program, served on the steering committee for Project Learning Tree, and is a member of the Wyoming Wool Growers and Stock Growers associations. She wrote that she is married to Jerry Dilts, a retired rancher, and that they own a small farm and raise cattle in Hidden Valley. She also wrote that she had served as a precinct committeewoman, was elected Fremont County Republican State Committeewoman in 2023, and had volunteered as a first responder.
